intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Experience New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience is the ultimate adrenaline rush, offering breathtaking views of the Central Otago landscape before you leap. Includes transport from Queenstown and a commemorative certificate.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most spectacular Great Walks, traversing alpine terrain between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland National Parks. The trail offers stunning views of glacial valleys, waterfalls, and mountain peaks. A two to three day hike covering 32km through pristine wilderness with DOC huts available along the route.

experiences.name: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic glacier valley at Franz Josef on the West Coast, getting up close to one of the world's most accessible glaciers. The self-guided valley floor walk winds through ancient rainforest and glacial moraine, offering incredible views of the ice face. Rangers provide safety briefings and the trail is well-marked.

experiences.name: Queenstown Gondola and Ben Lomond Summit Hike
experiences.description: Take the Skyline Gondola up to Bob's Peak then continue on foot to the Ben Lomond summit at 1748 meters for panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables mountain range. The full return hike is approximately 11km and takes 4 to 6 hours. Reward yourself with a meal at the summit restaurant on the way back down.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Combine a guided sea kayak paddle through the majestic Milford Sound fiord with a hike along part of the Milford Track, one of the world's greatest walks. Paddle beneath towering cliffs and Mitre Peak while watching for dolphins and seals, then explore the lush rainforest trails. A full-day guided experience that captures the raw beauty of Fiordland.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange ground transport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Grab a late-night snack from a 24-hour convenience store or airport vending machines.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Late-night snack from airport convenience store or 24-hour petrol station shop near resort (budget ~NZD $10)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer or book a Super Shuttle in advance to save money vs taxis. Download offline maps for South Island before landing. Exchange some NZD cash at the airport for small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a slow morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a walk along the beachfront to get your bearings. Explore the local area around the resort on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into central Christchurch (approx 30-40 min by public bus from coastal area). Visit the free Christchurch Botanic Gardens and walk through Hagley Park. Explore the Re:START container mall and the colorful street art of the city rebuild.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Avon River Precinct in the evening light. Return to resort via public bus. Relax at the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort or nearby bakery - budget ~NZD $8-12
meals.lunch: Pak'nSave or Countdown supermarket meal deal in Christchurch city - budget ~NZD $8-10
meals.dinner: Christchurch Night Noodle Markets or a local fish and chip shop near the beachfront - budget ~NZD $12-15

day_by_day.notes: Buy a Metrocard for Christchurch buses to save on fares. The Botanic Gardens and most city walks are completely free. Stock up on groceries for the trip at Pak'nSave - cheapest supermarket in NZ.

day_by_day.morning: Early start - drive or take a bus toward Arthur's Pass (approx 1.5 hours from Christchurch). Stop at Porters Pass lookout for stunning alpine views. Begin the Devil's Punchbowl Waterfall Walk (1 hour return, free) near Arthur's Pass village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Avalanche Peak Track (4-6 hours return, free DOC track) from Arthur's Pass village. This is a challenging but rewarding hike with panoramic Southern Alps views. Alternatively, do the easier Temple Basin walk if energy is low from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Christchurch / resort area. Cook a simple pasta dinner using supermarket supplies. Early night to prepare for the road trip ahead.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast from resort - muesli bars and fruit - budget ~NZD $5
meals.lunch: Packed sandwiches made from supermarket supplies eaten at Arthur's Pass - budget ~NZD $6-8
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta or rice dish at resort kitchen - budget ~NZD $8-10

day_by_day.notes: Arthur's Pass National Park entry and all DOC tracks are free. Wear layers as alpine weather changes rapidly even in November. Carry at least 2L of water per person. Check DOC website for track conditions before heading out.

day_by_day.morning: Pack up and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Begin the scenic drive south along State Highway 1 toward Aoraki/Mount Cook. Stop at Lake Tekapo (approx 3.5 hours from Christchurch). Visit the iconic Church of the Good Shepherd (free) and the turquoise lake shores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving to Aoraki/Mount Cook Village (approx 1.5 hours from Tekapo). Check into Mount Cook YHA or DOC campsite for budget accommodation. Begin the Kea Point Track (2 hours return, free) for close-up views of the Mueller Glacier and Mount Cook.
day_by_day.evening: Walk the short Bowen Bush Walk near the village. Stargaze from the village - the Mackenzie Basin is a Dark Sky Reserve. Cook dinner at YHA communal kitchen.

meals.breakfast: Supermarket supplies - toast, eggs, coffee at resort before checkout - budget ~NZD $8
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Lake Tekapo lakeside - budget ~NZD $8
meals.dinner: Self-catered at YHA kitchen - canned soup, bread, cheese - budget ~NZD $10-12

day_by_day.notes: Book YHA Mount Cook or DOC campsite in advance - November is peak season. Mount Cook YHA dorm beds from ~NZD $35/night. All DOC walks in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park are free. Fuel up at Tekapo as petrol is expensive at Mount Cook.

day_by_day.morning: Early 5:30am start for the Hooker Valley Track (3 hours return, free) - the most iconic walk in New Zealand. Cross three swing bridges to reach Hooker Lake with icebergs and direct views of Aoraki/Mount Cook. This is best done early to beat crowds and catch morning alpenglow.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Hooker Valley Track, rest and have lunch. In the afternoon, attempt the Mueller Hut Route (8-10 hours return, free but challenging) if energy and fitness allow, or alternatively hike the Red Tarns Track (2 hours return) for panoramic valley views.
day_by_day.evening: Cook dinner at YHA. Share stories with fellow budget travelers. Prepare gear for the drive to the West Coast tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Very early packed breakfast - energy bars, banana, instant coffee before the hike - budget ~NZD $5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Hooker Lake - sandwiches and snacks - budget ~NZD $8
meals.dinner: YHA communal kitchen - stir-fry with rice and vegetables - budget ~NZD $10-12

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is free and suitable for most fitness levels. Start before 6am for the best light and fewest crowds. Mueller Hut Route requires alpine experience and appropriate gear. Weather in November can include afternoon clouds - morning starts are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Mount Cook early and drive over Haast Pass toward the West Coast (approx 5-6 hours total drive). Stop at Blue Pools Walk near Haast Pass (45 min return, free) - stunning turquoise glacial pools. Continue through Haast township.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Fox Glacier area. Check into Fox Glacier Holiday Park or budget backpackers. Do the Lake Matheson Walk (1.5 hours return, free) for the famous mirror reflection of Mount Cook and Mount Tasman in the still lake - best in late afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Drive 25km north to Franz Josef township for dinner. Explore the small town. Return to Fox Glacier accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast eaten on the road at a scenic pull-off - budget ~NZD $6
meals.lunch: Haast township cafe or packed lunch by the Blue Pools - budget ~NZD $10-12
meals.dinner: Budget pizza or burger at a Franz Josef township cafe - budget ~NZD $15-18

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Mount Cook to Fox Glacier via Haast Pass is one of the most scenic in New Zealand - allow extra time for stops. Lake Matheson entry is free. Fox Glacier Holiday Park tent sites from ~NZD $20/night, dorm beds ~NZD $30-35/night.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Franz Josef Glacier. Begin the FEATURED EXPERIENCE: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk. Hike through the dramatic glacier valley getting up close to one of New Zealand's most accessible glaciers. The valley walk is free via DOC and takes approximately 2-3 hours return. Follow the marked trail to the glacier terminal face viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Franz Josef area. Walk the Sentinel Rock Track (30 min return, free) for elevated views of the glacier valley. Visit the DOC Franz Josef Visitor Centre (free) to learn about the glacier's history and retreat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fox Glacier accommodation. Cook dinner at the holiday park kitchen. Enjoy the rainforest sounds of the West Coast evening.

meals.breakfast: Holiday park kitchen - eggs on toast - budget ~NZD $8
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten in the glacier valley - budget ~NZD $8
meals.dinner: Self-catered at holiday park - pasta bolognese - budget ~NZD $10-12

day_by_day.notes: The Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk is completely free via DOC. Do NOT go beyond the marked barriers - glacier calving is extremely dangerous. The glacier has retreated significantly so the free valley walk still provides impressive views. Helicopter flights over the glacier are available but expensive (~NZD $250+) - skip for budget travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Depart West Coast and begin the long but spectacular drive to Queenstown via State Highway 6 south through Haast and then inland (approx 5-6 hours). Stop at Knights Point Lookout (free) for dramatic coastal views over the Tasman Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving through Wanaka. Stop at Lake Wanaka for a 30-minute break and walk along the lakefront. See the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' - the lone willow growing from the lake. Continue 45 minutes to Queenstown.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Queenstown. Check into Haka Lodge, Base Backpackers, or Nomads Queenstown for budget dorm accommodation (~NZD $35-45/night). Walk the Queenstown waterfront and explore the lively town center. Enjoy the buzzing atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Holiday park kitchen - cereal and fruit - budget ~NZD $5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at a scenic West Coast pullout - budget ~NZD $8
meals.dinner: Fergburger Queenstown - iconic and surprisingly affordable for Queenstown - budget ~NZD $15-18

day_by_day.notes: Fergburger in Queenstown is a must-do budget meal and a NZ institution - expect a queue but worth it. Book Queenstown hostel well in advance as November is busy. The drive through Haast Pass and along the West Coast is spectacular - leave early to allow photo stops.

day_by_day.morning: FEATURED EXPERIENCE: Queenstown Gondola and Ben Lomond Summit Hike. Take the Skyline Gondola up to Bob's Peak (gondola ~NZD $36 return - budget splurge worth it). From Bob's Peak, continue on foot along the Ben Lomond Track to the summit at 1748 meters. The full hike from the gondola top station takes approximately 4-5 hours return.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Ben Lomond summit hike - pushing to the top rewards you with 360-degree views of Queenstown, Lake Wakatipu, and the Remarkables mountain range. This is one of the best free hikes accessible from Queenstown town center.
day_by_day.evening: Descend back to Bob's Peak and take the gondola down. Soak tired legs in the Queenstown waterfront. Explore the Queenstown Night Markets (Saturdays) or grab affordable dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen - toast and peanut butter - budget ~NZD $4
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Ben Lomond summit - sandwiches and energy bars - budget ~NZD $8
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market or Pak'nSave self-catered - budget ~NZD $12-15

day_by_day.notes: The Ben Lomond Track beyond the gondola top station is free. The gondola ticket (~NZD $36) is the main cost. Wear proper hiking boots and bring warm layers - the summit can be cold and windy even in November. Start early to avoid afternoon clouds. Total elevation gain from gondola top is approximately 600m.

day_by_day.morning: BUNGEE JUMPING DAY! Head to the AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungy (43m, ~NZD $165-195) - the world's first commercial bungy jump site. Book online in advance for the best price. This is the budget-friendly bungy option compared to the Nevis (~NZD $275). The historic bridge setting over the Kawarau River is iconic.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, walk the Kawarau Bridge area trails (free). Drive or bus back to Queenstown. Visit the free Queenstown Gardens - walk the rose garden and lakefront trails. Rent a bike from Queenstown Bike Hire (~NZD $20/hour) to explore the lakefront trail.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungy jump at a Queenstown bar during happy hour (many bars have 5-7pm specials). Try the Minus 5 Ice Bar for a splurge or keep it budget with a supermarket beer by the lake.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen - porridge with banana - budget ~NZD $4
meals.lunch: Subway or a food court option in Queenstown central - budget ~NZD $12
meals.dinner: Winnies Pizza Queenstown or self-catered at hostel - budget ~NZD $15-18

day_by_day.notes: Book Kawarau bungy online at least 3-5 days in advance and look for online discount codes (sometimes 10-15% off). The jump includes a video and photo package for an extra cost - skip the package to save money and just enjoy the experience. The Kawarau Bridge is a 20-minute drive from Queenstown center.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning hike up the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (2-3 hours return, free). This accessible hike starts from town and offers panoramic views over Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu. A great free alternative to the gondola for morning views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a scenic bus to Glenorchy (45 min from Queenstown, free road). Walk the Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway (1 hour return, free) through wetlands with stunning views of the Dart River valley and Richardson Mountains. This is Lord of the Rings filming territory.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Visit the Remarkables Lookout at sunset (free, short drive). Cook dinner at hostel or grab cheap takeaways.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen - eggs and toast - budget ~NZD $5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Glenorchy - eat by the lake - budget ~NZD $8
meals.dinner: Self-catered hostel meal - fried rice with vegetables and eggs - budget ~NZD $8-10

day_by_day.notes: The drive to Glenorchy along Lake Wakatipu is free and stunning - often called one of the most beautiful short drives in New Zealand. Glenorchy township has a small cafe but bring packed lunch to save money. The Dart River valley was used as Isengard and Lothlórien in Lord of the Rings.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Queenstown to Milford Sound day trip bus (approx NZD $120-150 return including cruise - book through Real NZ or Intercity for best budget rates). Depart Queenstown at 7:30am. Drive through the stunning Eglinton Valley and Te Anau.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Milford Sound. Take the 2-hour Milford Sound cruise (included in most day trip packages or ~NZD $65-80 standalone). See Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, Bowen Falls, and watch for dolphins, seals, and penguins. The scenery is absolutely world-class.
day_by_day.evening: Return bus journey to Queenstown (arrive back approximately 8-9pm). Grab a late dinner from a takeaway shop. Pack bags for the final day.

meals.breakfast: Early hostel kitchen breakfast before 7am departure - budget ~NZD $5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the bus or Milford Sound cafe (expensive) - bring your own to save money - budget ~NZD $8-10
meals.dinner: Late night takeaways in Queenstown - fish and chips - budget ~NZD $12-15

day_by_day.notes: Milford Sound day trips are long (14+ hours) but absolutely worth it. Book well in advance as they sell out in November. The cruise is the highlight - sit outside on the deck for the best views and wildlife spotting. Milford Sound receives 7-8m of rain per year - waterfalls are actually more impressive on rainy days so don't be deterred by wet weather.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Check out of hostel and store luggage. Do the free Queenstown Waterfront Walk along Lake Wakatipu one last time. Browse the Queenstown markets if it's Saturday or explore Earnslaw Park. Visit the Kiwi Birdlife Park (NZD $52 entry) OR save money and spot free wildlife at the Queenstown waterfront where wild ducks and paradise shelducks are common.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir shopping at the Queenstown Night Market or Remarkables Market for affordable NZ-made gifts. Head to the airport for departure or continue to next destination. If departing from Christchurch, begin the 8-hour drive north or book an Intercity bus.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or transfer to next accommodation. Reflect on an incredible 13 days exploring the South Island's best free hikes, glaciers, and adrenaline experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final hostel breakfast or a proper cafe treat - budget ~NZD $12-15
meals.lunch: Pak'nSave packed lunch for the road or airport - budget ~NZD $8-10
meals.dinner: Airport meal or packed supplies for travel - budget ~NZD $12-15

day_by_day.notes: If flying out of Queenstown, the airport is only 10 minutes from town. If flying from Christchurch, allow a full day for the drive. Total estimated budget for 13 days excluding flights and accommodation: approximately NZD $800-1100 covering food, transport, bungy jump, gondola, and Milford Sound day trip. The South Island's greatest assets - its national parks and hiking trails - are almost entirely free.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch or Queenstown airport at 22:30. Collect luggage, arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Grab a light snack from the hotel if available.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight
meals.dinner: Late-night hotel snack or 24-hour convenience store near the resort

day_by_day.notes: Late arrival day — no activities scheduled. Confirm your booking details with the resort front desk and pick up any local maps or brochures. Get a good night's rest to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning exploring the beachfront area on foot — take a relaxed walk along the shore to get your bearings and soak in the South Island scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or arrange a short transfer into the nearest town centre. Visit a local visitor information centre to confirm bookings and collect trail maps. Explore local shops, pick up any hiking gear or supplies you may need for the days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed evening. Stroll along the beachfront at sunset and enjoy the views.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — enjoy a full New Zealand spread to fuel up
meals.lunch: Casual café in town — try a classic Kiwi meat pie or fresh sandwich (~NZD 15–20)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant near the resort — look for fresh South Island seafood such as green-lipped mussels or blue cod (~NZD 35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Orientation and recovery day. Use this time to confirm all activity bookings, check weather forecasts, and ensure you have appropriate clothing and footwear for upcoming hikes and adventure activities.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Queenstown Gondola and Ben Lomond Summit Hike. Take the Skyline Gondola up to Bob's Peak (a scenic ride with panoramic views over Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu), then begin the trail toward the Ben Lomond summit at 1748 metres.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the ascent to Ben Lomond summit. The full return hike from the gondola top terminal takes approximately 4–5 hours. Enjoy 360-degree views of the Remarkables, Cecil Peak, and Lake Wakatipu from the top before descending back to the gondola.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown town centre via gondola. Freshen up and explore the vibrant Queenstown waterfront and lakefront area.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch — sandwiches, energy bars, fruit, and plenty of water from a local supermarket or bakery
meals.dinner: Queenstown waterfront restaurant — try Fergburger (iconic NZ burger joint, ~NZD 15–20) or a sit-down meal at a lakefront bistro (~NZD 35–50)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy hiking boots and bring layers — the Ben Lomond summit can be cold and windy even in November. Start early to avoid afternoon cloud cover. Total hike distance is approximately 11 km return from the gondola terminal. Check the gondola operating hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort after the big hike. Enjoy breakfast and a gentle beachfront walk. Use the morning to recharge and prepare for the Nevis Bungy Jump experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Nevis Bungy Jump — New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 metres above the Nevis River gorge. Transfer from Queenstown is included with most bookings. Experience the heart-pounding freefall and take in the dramatic canyon scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown or the resort. Celebrate your jump with a well-deserved dinner and drinks. Share photos and relive the experience.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fuel up well before the jump
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Queenstown before departing for the Nevis — avoid eating too heavily before the jump (~NZD 15–20)
meals.dinner: Celebrate at a mid-range Queenstown restaurant — try a local craft brewery gastropub for burgers, pizza, and NZ craft beer (~NZD 35–50)

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy Jump is operated by AJ Hackett. Transfers depart from the Queenstown booking office. Weight limits apply (45–127 kg). Book well in advance as this is extremely popular in summer. Participants receive a certificate and can purchase video/photo packages on-site (~NZD 40–60 extra).

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the West Coast — drive the scenic route toward Franz Josef Glacier. The drive from Queenstown area takes approximately 4–5 hours via Haast Pass, one of New Zealand's most spectacular mountain highways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Franz Josef township. Check into overnight accommodation (budget for a mid-range hotel or lodge, ~NZD 120–180/night). After settling in, begin the Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk — hike through the dramatic glacier valley, getting up close to the terminal face of one of the world's most accessible glaciers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Franz Josef township. Explore the small village and relax after the long driving day.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a café in Haast township during the Haast Pass drive (~NZD 15–20)
meals.dinner: Franz Josef township restaurant — try the Blue Ice Restaurant for hearty West Coast fare such as venison or whitebait fritters (~NZD 35–50)

day_by_day.notes: The Haast Pass drive is stunning but take your time — there are numerous photo stops including Thunder Creek Falls and the Gates of Haast. The Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk is self-guided and free. The glacier face is constantly changing so follow all DOC safety signage and stay behind barriers. Wear waterproof footwear as the valley floor can be wet.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning exploring more of the Franz Josef area. Consider a short hike to the Roberts Point Track lookout or the Sentinel Rock walk for elevated glacier views. Alternatively, visit Lake Wombat for a peaceful forest and lake walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the drive south toward Te Anau — the gateway to Milford Sound and Fiordland. The drive takes approximately 5–6 hours. Enjoy the changing landscapes from the West Coast rainforest to the Southland plains.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Te Anau. Check into your accommodation (mid-range lakeside motel or hotel, ~NZD 120–160/night). Walk along the shores of Lake Te Anau at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Franz Josef café breakfast — try eggs benedict with locally smoked salmon (~NZD 18–25)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop en route
meals.dinner: Te Anau restaurant — try the Sandfly Café or a lakeside bistro for local lamb or venison (~NZD 35–50)

day_by_day.notes: This is a significant driving day (~5–6 hours). Break the journey with stops and don't rush the West Coast departure — the morning glacier walk is worth the extra time. Fuel up in Fox Glacier or Haast as petrol stations are sparse. Te Anau is the base for Milford Sound and Fiordland activities.

day_by_day.morning: Full day for the Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo. Depart Te Anau early for the 1.5-hour scenic drive to Milford Sound along State Highway 94 — one of the world's most beautiful drives. Begin the guided sea kayak paddle through the majestic Milford Sound fiord, paddling beneath towering peaks and Mitre Peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, join the hike along part of the Milford Track or a guided nature walk in Fiordland National Park. Look for fur seals, dolphins, and Fiordland crested penguins. Absorb the dramatic scenery of sheer cliff faces and cascading waterfalls.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Te Anau. Enjoy a well-earned dinner and reflect on an extraordinary day in one of the world's great natural wonders.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Te Anau accommodation before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the tour operator or bring your own — eat at Milford Sound with the fiord as your backdrop
meals.dinner: Te Anau restaurant — treat yourself to a proper sit-down dinner after a big activity day (~NZD 40–55)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo well in advance — this is one of the most popular experiences in NZ. The drive through Homer Tunnel is spectacular. Sandflies are notorious at Milford Sound — bring strong insect repellent. Waterproof gear is essential as Milford receives over 7 metres of rain annually. November is generally good but be prepared for rain.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning in Te Anau. Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves (book a morning tour) — a magical underground experience featuring glowworm grotto accessed by boat (~NZD 55–75 per person). Alternatively, take a peaceful walk along the Te Anau lakefront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward Queenstown (approximately 2 hours). Stop at Kingston and enjoy views of Lake Wakatipu. Arrive in Queenstown and check back into resort accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's lively Shotover Street and waterfront. Browse local galleries and souvenir shops.

meals.breakfast: Te Anau café breakfast (~NZD 18–25)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at Kingston café on the drive back
meals.dinner: Queenstown — try a mid-range restaurant on the Mall for wood-fired pizza or NZ lamb rack (~NZD 40–55)

day_by_day.notes: The Te Anau Glowworm Caves tour must be pre-booked through Real Journeys/RealNZ. If skipping the caves, use the morning for a final Fiordland walk before departing. The drive back to Queenstown is relaxed and scenic.

day_by_day.morning: Prepare for the multi-day Routeburn Track Great Walk. Pack your gear, collect any rental equipment, and arrange transport to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead (approximately 1 hour from Queenstown). Begin hiking the Routeburn Track — Day 1 of the Great Walk, heading toward Routeburn Flats Hut through ancient beech forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking through the Routeburn Valley. Arrive at Routeburn Flats Hut (approximately 2.5 hours from the trailhead). Explore the surrounding flats and enjoy views of the surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Routeburn Flats Hut (DOC Great Walk hut, ~NZD 65/night). Cook dinner in the hut kitchen, meet fellow trampers, and enjoy the peaceful mountain atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before transfer to trailhead
meals.lunch: Trail lunch from your pack — sandwiches, crackers, cheese, dried fruit
meals.dinner: Self-catered hut dinner — pre-prepared dehydrated meal or packed ingredients (plan and purchase all food in Queenstown before departure)

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track is a DOC Great Walk requiring advance hut bookings (book months ahead, especially for November/summer season). Hut bookings are made through the DOC website. Pack all food, a good sleeping bag, rain gear, and trekking poles. The track is well-marked but weather can change rapidly. Estimated Day 1 hiking: 7.5 km, 2–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early at Routeburn Flats Hut. After breakfast, continue the Routeburn Track toward Routeburn Falls Hut — a steady climb through stunning alpine terrain with views of the valley below. Arrive at Routeburn Falls Hut (approximately 1.5 hours from Flats Hut).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the most spectacular section of the track — cross the alpine Harris Saddle (1255 m) with panoramic views across Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Park. Descend toward Lake Mackenzie Hut through tussock grasslands and subalpine scrub.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Lake Mackenzie Hut (approximately 4–5 hours from Falls Hut). Enjoy the stunning lakeside setting with reflections of the surrounding peaks. Relax, cook dinner, and socialise with fellow hikers.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered hut breakfast — oats, muesli, coffee
meals.lunch: Trail lunch on Harris Saddle — take time to enjoy the views
meals.dinner: Self-catered hut dinner — dehydrated meal or pre-packed ingredients

day_by_day.notes: This is the most demanding day of the Routeburn Track. Harris Saddle can be exposed and cold even in summer — always carry full wet weather gear and warm layers. The views from the saddle on a clear day are among the finest in New Zealand. Total distance: approximately 11 km, 5–6 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Final day on the Routeburn Track. Depart Lake Mackenzie Hut after breakfast and hike the final section toward the Divide — passing through the Earland Falls (174 m drop — spectacular) and through more beech forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at The Divide (the track's western terminus) after approximately 3–4 hours of hiking. Arrange pre-booked transport back to Te Anau or Queenstown (shuttle buses run from The Divide). Return to Queenstown and check back into resort accommodation. Shower, rest, and celebrate completing the Great Walk.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Queenstown to mark completing the Routeburn Track.

meals.breakfast: Final hut breakfast — use up remaining trail food
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch for the final trail section
meals.dinner: Queenstown celebration dinner — treat yourself to a proper restaurant meal with NZ wine (~NZD 50–70 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your shuttle from The Divide back to Queenstown or Te Anau through Tracknet or similar operators. The shuttle must be arranged before starting the track. Total Routeburn Track: approximately 32 km over 3 days. This is one of New Zealand's finest multi-day hikes — a genuine highlight of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the Routeburn Track. Sleep in, enjoy a long resort breakfast, and take a gentle walk along the beachfront. Visit a Queenstown day spa for a massage or soak to recover tired muscles (~NZD 80–120).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Queenstown at leisure. Visit the Kiwi Birdlife Park to see kiwi, kea, and other native NZ wildlife (~NZD 50). Browse the Queenstown Arts & Crafts Market (if running on this date) or explore local galleries. Consider a scenic Lake Wakatipu cruise on the historic TSS Earnslaw steamship (~NZD 55).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Queenstown — enjoy sundowners at a lakefront bar watching the sunset over the Remarkables mountain range.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent resort breakfast — full cooked breakfast to celebrate completing the track
meals.lunch: Queenstown café lunch — avocado toast, fresh salads, or a hearty bowl (~NZD 20–30)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a quality Queenstown restaurant — try The Bunker or Rata for contemporary NZ cuisine using local ingredients (~NZD 60–80 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is your wind-down and reflection day. Use it to purchase any last-minute souvenirs, NZ merino wool products, or local food items to take home. Confirm your departure logistics for tomorrow and ensure all gear is cleaned and packed.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the South Island. Enjoy a last resort breakfast and take one final walk along the beachfront to soak in the scenery. Pack and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, spend remaining time in Queenstown. Visit any final spots you may have missed — the Queenstown Gardens, Frankton Arm, or a final coffee at a favourite café. Head to the airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart New Zealand South Island, carrying memories of bungy jumps, glacier walks, fiords, and the magnificent Routeburn Track.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — savour the last New Zealand morning
meals.lunch: Airport café or final Queenstown lunch before departure (~NZD 20–30)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at least 2 hours before international departure (2.5 hours recommended). Return any rental gear, settle any outstanding bills, and complete biosecurity checks — NZ has strict rules about food items leaving the country. Ensure hiking boots are clean and free of soil for biosecurity compliance.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Experience New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience is the ultimate adrenaline rush, offering breathtaking views of the Central Otago landscape before you leap. Includes transport from Queenstown and a commemorative certificate.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most spectacular Great Walks, traversing alpine terrain between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland National Parks. The trail offers stunning views of glacial valleys, waterfalls, and mountain peaks. A two to three day hike covering 32km through pristine wilderness with DOC huts available along the route.

experiences.name: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic glacier valley at Franz Josef on the West Coast, getting up close to one of the world's most accessible glaciers. The self-guided valley floor walk winds through ancient rainforest and glacial moraine, offering incredible views of the ice face. Rangers provide safety briefings and the trail is well-marked.

experiences.name: Queenstown Gondola and Ben Lomond Summit Hike
experiences.description: Take the Skyline Gondola up to Bob's Peak then continue on foot to the Ben Lomond summit at 1748 meters for panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables mountain range. The full return hike is approximately 11km and takes 4 to 6 hours. Reward yourself with a meal at the summit restaurant on the way back down.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Combine a guided sea kayak paddle through the majestic Milford Sound fiord with a hike along part of the Milford Track, one of the world's greatest walks. Paddle beneath towering cliffs and Mitre Peak while watching for dolphins and seals, then explore the lush rainforest trails. A full-day guided experience that captures the raw beauty of Fiordland.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind with a welcome amenity and nightcap at the resort bar.

meals.breakfast: N/A - in-flight or airport
meals.lunch: N/A - in-flight or airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night supper arranged by the resort upon arrival - charcuterie board and New Zealand Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc in-room

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. Resort concierge should be notified of late arrival. Keep Day 1 completely relaxed to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast with views of the surrounding landscape. Explore the resort grounds and beachfront area. Orientation walk around the local Queenstown waterfront and town centre to acclimatise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Queenstown Gondola and Ben Lomond Summit Hike - Take the Skyline Gondola up to Bob's Peak, then embark on the stunning hike to Ben Lomond summit at 1,748 metres. Enjoy panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables mountain range. Allow approximately 4-5 hours for the full summit hike.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a shower and refresh. Sunset cocktails on the resort terrace overlooking the lake. Elegant dinner at a top Queenstown restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort - eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh fruit, artisan pastries and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the resort for the Ben Lomond hike - gourmet sandwiches, local cheeses, fruit and energy snacks
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant, Queenstown - acclaimed fine dining by Chef Josh Emett featuring premium New Zealand produce and an extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book Skyline Gondola tickets in advance. Wear layered hiking clothing as summit temperatures can be significantly cooler. Sturdy hiking boots essential. Gondola operates until late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump - Experience New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 metres above the Nevis River gorge with AJ Hackett. A thrilling, iconic adventure activity. Transfer to the Nevis Valley site takes approximately 45 minutes from Queenstown. Morning session recommended for calmer conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-adrenaline recovery with a scenic drive through the Crown Range Road, the highest sealed road in New Zealand, stopping at Cardrona for a heritage pub experience. Browse Arrowtown's charming gold-rush era village, boutiques and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for a relaxing spa treatment at the resort. Premium dinner celebrating the day's achievement.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before the Nevis jump - fruit, yoghurt, toast and coffee. Avoid heavy meals before the jump.
meals.lunch: The Cardrona Hotel - historic 1863 pub with hearty New Zealand fare, craft beers and a charming garden setting
meals.dinner: Fishbone Bar & Grill, Queenstown - celebrated seafood restaurant with premium New Zealand fish, crayfish and oysters paired with Central Otago Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy must be pre-booked well in advance - extremely popular. Weight restrictions apply (45-127kg). Participants must sign waiver. Video and photo package recommended as a keepsake. Wear comfortable, secure clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Private scenic helicopter flight over the Remarkables, Lake Wakatipu and surrounding fiordland landscapes. Touch down on a remote alpine peak for a champagne morning tea experience with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo - Depart Queenstown for the scenic drive to Milford Sound (approximately 4 hours, stopping at The Divide and Mirror Lakes). Join the guided sea kayak paddle through the majestic Milford Sound fiord combined with a hike along part of the Milford Track.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight stay at Milford Sound Lodge or return journey to Queenstown with private transfer. Sunset over the fiord is spectacular in November.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before early departure - continental spread with New Zealand honey, local yoghurts and fresh seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Milford Sound - premium hamper provided by the tour operator featuring local produce, artisan bread and New Zealand wines
meals.dinner: Milford Sound Lodge Pio Pio Restaurant (if staying overnight) - fresh seafood and local cuisine with fiordland views, OR dinner at The Bunker Restaurant, Queenstown upon return

day_by_day.notes: The drive to Milford Sound is one of the world's most scenic - depart early (6:00-6:30am) to maximise time. November weather in Milford can be wet - pack waterproof gear. Sandfly repellent is essential. Pre-book kayak and hike combo well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning at the resort following the Milford Sound day. Enjoy a spa session with a deep tissue massage or hot stone therapy. Gentle swim or relaxation by the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private wine tour of the Central Otago wine region - one of the world's most acclaimed Pinot Noir producing areas. Visit Amisfield Winery, Peregrine Wines and Gibbston Valley Winery with a private sommelier guide. Barrel room tours and exclusive tastings included.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard a private charter vessel. Canapés and Central Otago wines served on board as the Remarkables glow in the evening light.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full resort breakfast - eggs your way, smoked salmon, avocado, fresh-pressed juices and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Amisfield Winery Restaurant - celebrated paddock-to-plate dining with a set menu that changes with the seasons, perfectly paired with estate wines
meals.dinner: Canapés and wine on the sunset lake cruise, followed by a late dinner at Botswana Butchery, Queenstown - premium cuts of New Zealand grass-fed beef and lamb with lake views

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the private wine tour and lake cruise. November is a beautiful time in Central Otago with vineyards in full leaf. Designated driver or private transfer essential for the wine tour. The lake cruise is weather-dependent - have a backup plan.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Great Walk - Day 1 of a 2-day guided Routeburn Track experience. Depart Queenstown early for the Routeburn Shelter trailhead (approximately 1.5 hours). Begin hiking through ancient beech forests towards the Routeburn Flats and Routeburn Falls Hut. Approximately 8km, 4-5 hours hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking to Routeburn Falls Hut area. Explore the dramatic alpine scenery above the bushline. The falls themselves are a spectacular highlight. Guided interpretation of the unique flora and fauna of the Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at Routeburn Falls Lodge (exclusive guided category with private facilities and gourmet meals) or helicopter out for a luxury lodge stay. Stargazing in the pristine dark skies of the national park.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure - high-energy options including porridge, eggs, fresh fruit and coffee
meals.lunch: Trail lunch provided by the guided tour operator - gourmet packed lunch with sandwiches, snacks, fruit and energy bars consumed on the track
meals.dinner: Routeburn Falls Lodge guided category dinner - three-course meal with New Zealand wines served in the lodge dining room with other guided walkers

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ultimate Hikes guided Routeburn Track experience well in advance - premium guided category fills quickly. Pack light as porters carry main luggage. Bring layers, waterproofs and quality hiking boots. November is an excellent month for the Routeburn - wildflowers and long daylight hours.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Great Walk - Day 2. Hike from Routeburn Falls to Harris Saddle and Lake Harris - the dramatic alpine highlight of the track at 1,255 metres. Breathtaking 360-degree views across Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks on a clear day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the alpine ridge to the Conical Hill lookout (optional side trip to 1,515m) and descend through the Hollyford Valley to the Divide. Private transfer back to Queenstown. Debrief with guides and celebrate the achievement.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Luxurious hot bath or spa treatment to ease hiking muscles. Celebratory dinner at Queenstown's finest restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hot cooked breakfast at Routeburn Falls Lodge before the day's hiking - eggs, bacon, toast, cereals, juice and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch at Lake Harris - enjoy the meal with one of New Zealand's most spectacular alpine lake backdrops
meals.dinner: Palazzo del Capitano or Amisfield Bistro - celebrate completing the Routeburn with a premium degustation dinner with matched wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Harris Saddle can be exposed to strong winds and weather changes - layers and waterproofs essential even in November. The Conical Hill side trip adds approximately 1 hour but is highly recommended for clear days. Total Day 2 hiking approximately 11km.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day at the resort. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast and take advantage of the resort's luxury amenities - pool, spa, gym or simply relax on the beachfront. Optional gentle walk along the Queenstown lakefront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Queenstown's premium shopping and arts scene. Visit local galleries featuring New Zealand artists and craftspeople. Browse boutiques along the Mall and Beach Street for New Zealand-made luxury goods, merino wool products and pounamu (greenstone) jewellery.
day_by_day.evening: Private dining experience - arrange a private chef dinner at the resort or a special chef's table experience at a top Queenstown restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent resort brunch - full spread including eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, fruit platters, mimosas and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Rātā or Bespoke Kitchen - casual premium lunch in town, featuring seasonal New Zealand produce and craft beverages
meals.dinner: Chef's table experience at The Sherwood or a private in-resort dining experience with a dedicated chef and personalised menu

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest day after two consecutive days of intensive hiking on the Routeburn Track. Allow the body to recover fully. Use this time for any gear maintenance, laundry or trip admin. Book any remaining experiences for the second week.

day_by_day.morning: Private 4WD off-road adventure tour through the Queenstown backcountry and high country stations. Explore remote landscapes inaccessible to regular vehicles, including river crossings, alpine tussock lands and historic gold-mining areas with an expert local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk preparation - private luxury transfer departs Queenstown heading north along the West Coast (approximately 4-5 hours, one of New Zealand's most scenic drives). Stop at Haast Pass and the Blue Pools for a short walk.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Franz Josef village. Check in to Te Waonui Forest Retreat (if changing accommodation) or arrange premium lodge accommodation. Dinner in Franz Josef.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure - eggs, fresh fruit, pastries and coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Haast Pass or Blue Pools - gourmet hamper prepared by the resort for the road journey
meals.dinner: The Landing Restaurant at Te Waonui Forest Retreat, Franz Josef - rainforest setting with premium New Zealand cuisine and West Coast seafood specialties

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Queenstown to Franz Josef via Haast Pass is approximately 4.5-5 hours. Consider breaking the journey at Wanaka for a short stop and coffee. The Blue Pools walk at Haast is approximately 45 minutes return and highly recommended. Book Franz Josef accommodation well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk - Guided hike through the dramatic glacier valley, getting up close to one of the world's most accessible glaciers. Walk through ancient rainforest, across glacial outwash plains and up to the glacier terminal face. Guided interpretation of the unique geology and ecology.
day_by_day.afternoon: Helicopter glacier experience - take a scenic helicopter flight over Franz Josef and Fox Glaciers with a snow landing on the upper glacier neve. Walk on the ancient ice with crampons provided. Dramatic aerial views of the Southern Alps and Tasman Sea coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the lodge and enjoy the unique experience of being surrounded by temperate rainforest. Evening walk on the nature trails around the lodge to spot native wildlife including kiwi (guided night walk available).

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast before the glacier walk - hot options, fresh fruit, cereals and coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the glacier valley or at a scenic viewpoint - provided by the tour operator
meals.dinner: Te Waonui Forest Retreat restaurant - degustation menu featuring West Coast whitebait, local seafood and premium New Zealand meats with matched wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Franz Josef Glacier has been retreating significantly - the helicopter snow landing on the upper glacier is the best way to experience the ice up close. Book both the valley walk and helicopter experience in advance. Weather can change rapidly on the West Coast - have flexible plans. Sandfly repellent essential.

day_by_day.morning: Morning kayak or stand-up paddleboard on Lake Mapourika near Franz Josef - one of New Zealand's most pristine lakes with stunning Southern Alps reflections. Guided nature tour of the temperate rainforest surrounding the lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive south along the West Coast to Fox Glacier for an additional glacier perspective and the famous Fox Glacier lookout. Continue to Gillespies Beach for a walk to the historic miner's hut and seal colony. Begin the return journey south.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey towards Queenstown or Wanaka. Overnight stop in Wanaka - check in to Edgewater Hotel or Wanaka's finest boutique accommodation. Lakeside dinner in Wanaka.

meals.breakfast: Franz Josef lodge breakfast - full hot breakfast with local produce before check-out
meals.lunch: Fox Glacier cafe or packed lunch from the lodge for the journey - enjoy at Gillespies Beach
meals.dinner: Bistro Gentil, Wanaka - acclaimed fine dining with Lake Wanaka views, featuring premium New Zealand produce and an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Gillespies Beach is approximately 20km from Fox Glacier on an unsealed road - suitable for standard vehicles. The seal colony walk is approximately 1 hour return. November is perfect for the West Coast with long daylight hours. Wanaka is approximately 2.5 hours from Fox Glacier.

day_by_day.morning: Wanaka morning - hike the iconic Roy's Peak Track for breathtaking views over Lake Wanaka and Mount Aspiring National Park. The summit at 1,578 metres offers one of New Zealand's most photographed panoramas. Allow 5-6 hours for the full return hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Roy's Peak and freshen up. Visit the Wanaka Tree (the famous lone willow in the lake) and explore Wanaka's charming lakefront. Browse local galleries and the New Zealand Fighter Pilots Museum for a cultural interlude.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown (approximately 1 hour). Final evening at Aegean Bliss Resort. Sunset cocktails and a premium farewell dinner celebrating the entire South Island journey.

meals.breakfast: Early Wanaka hotel breakfast before the Roy's Peak hike - high-energy options essential
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch on Roy's Peak summit - arrange with the Wanaka hotel the evening before. Enjoy with spectacular 360-degree views.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Rata Restaurant or Botswana Butchery, Queenstown - premium New Zealand beef, lamb and seafood with a selection from Central Otago's finest Pinot Noirs

day_by_day.notes: Roy's Peak is a popular hike - start early (6:00-7:00am) to avoid crowds and secure the iconic summit photo. The track is well-marked but steep. Trekking poles recommended. November offers excellent visibility. This is a fitting final major hike of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Leisurely breakfast with lake views. Last-minute souvenir shopping in Queenstown - premium New Zealand merino wool products, pounamu jewellery, artisan foods and Central Otago wines to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time - optional final activity such as a short lakefront walk, jet boat ride on the Shotover River, or a final gondola ride for last views over Queenstown. Private luxury transfer to Queenstown Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Queenstown. Reflect on an extraordinary 13-day South Island adventure encompassing world-class hiking, New Zealand's highest bungy jump, glacier experiences, fiordland kayaking and the finest luxury hospitality the South Island has to offer.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast - indulgent spread with all the favourites accumulated over the trip
meals.lunch: Fergburger (Queenstown institution) or a final premium cafe lunch in town before airport transfer - a quintessential Queenstown send-off
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at Aegean Bliss Resort is typically 11:00am - arrange late check-out if possible given the afternoon departure. Ensure all purchased wines are properly packed for checked luggage. Allow at least 2.5 hours before international departure at Queenstown Airport. Consider purchasing travel insurance coverage for the entire trip.
